a fundamental understanding of the processes of P release from lake sediments and the application of this understanding to the management of lake eutrophication.
the development of a simple, inexpensive and rapid method for estimating P release potential from lake sediments.
the control of P release from lake sediments by Al.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the molar ratio of Al to P in the sediment is an important factor in determining the amount of P released from the sediments and that the Al/P ratio is a good indicator of the amount of Al needed to be added to the sediment to prevent P release.
Al dosing of lake sediment is a useful and effective means to prevent hypolimitic P release under reducing conditions.
the Al(OH)3:Fe(OH) 3 ratio in sediments is the most important factor in determining whether or not hypolimnetically released P will be present in the water column.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Al(OH)3 and Al3+ can be added to P rich sediments to control P release.
the ability of lake sediments to release P during anoxia is related to the relative concentrations of Fe(OH)3 and Al(OH)3 in the sediments.
Al(OH)3 is a better sediment treatment for reducing hypolimnetiC P release than Fe(OH)3, because Al(OH)2+ is the more effective P scavenging agent.

aluminum is a key control on the release of reactive (phosphorus-like) phosphorus from lake sediments.
